chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'Do you know from where the dowries of women became four thousand?' I said, 'No'. So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Indeed, Umm Habib, daughter of Abu Sufyan, was in Abyssinia. The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) proposed to her, and Al-Najashi sent to her on his behalf four thousand. From there, they take it as a precedent. As for the dower, it is twelve Oqiyah and one Nash.'
ai.seo_question: What is the historical origin of the four thousand dowry custom in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) traces the customary dowry of four thousand dirhams to the Prophet's marriage to Umm Habib in Abyssinia, where the Negus sent this amount on the Prophet's behalf, establishing a historical precedent for this valuation. The narration further codifies the standard dower as twelve Oqiyah and one Nash, reflecting the economic norms of the time and providing a benchmark for marital financial obligations in Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, form his father, from Hammad, from Hareyz, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said,

‘Abu Ja’farasws said: ‘Do you know from where the dowries of women came to be of four thousand?’ I said, ‘No’. So heasws said: ‘Umm Habeeb daughter of Abu Sufyan was in Ethiopia. So the Prophetsaww proposed to her and Al-Najashy sent four thousand to her on hissaww behalf. Thus, from then on they are taking by it. But as for the dower, so it is of twelve Owqiya and one Nashha (five hundred Dirhams)’.
en.sarwar: 13. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following:

“Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, once asked, ‘Do you know why mahr (dower) of women has become four thousand?’ I replied, ‘No, I do not know.’ He (the Imam) said, “Umm Habibah, daughter of abu Sufyan was in al-Habashah (Ethiopia) and the Holy Prophet, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, proposed marriage. Al-Najashiy paid four thousand. For this reason they take it, however, the actual mahr (dower) is twelve Awqiyah and one Nashsha.’”
